text:
Alex Rivera: Quick sync — I'm putting together the RFC for private deployments (VPC + on-prem networking). Need a consensus on acceptance criteria, security knobs, and rollout plan before Friday EOD. Ping @Maria, @Jamal, @Sophie, @Kevin for input.

Maria Chen: High-level constraints from infra: support two install modes — 1) VPC integration with private control plane (PrivateLink / TGW / peering) and 2) on-prem air-gapped installer. Customer-managed networking means we can't force NATs or public endpoints.

Jamal Singh: Security notes: must support BYOK (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault) and HSMs via PKCS#11. No outbound internet by default for air-gapped; installer needs to accept signed tarball + hashes. Mutual TLS for control plane traffic and mTLS for node-to-node. Audit logs pushed to customer SIEM over TLS (syslog/HTTPS).

Sophie Park: From CS: customers frequently ask for: static IP ranges they can allowlist, ability to insert their own LB (NLB/ALB) or route through an on-prem reverse proxy, and FIPS-capable crypto. Also they want a sample terraform module for networking.

Kevin Ortiz: Runtime concerns — streaming and KV cache rely on stable low-latency links between nodes. We need explicit acceptance criteria for packet loss, MTU, and headroom for 99th percentile latency. Also we should document required ports: 443 (control plane API), 8443 (runtime gRPC/ws), and optional 50051 for internal gRPC. Use TLS + ALPN for protocol negotiation. Avoid UDP heartbeats; use TCP keepalive to be safe for restrictive networks.

Maria Chen: Proposed acceptance criteria (draft):
- Connectivity modes: 
  - VPC mode: must work via AWS PrivateLink, VPC peering, or Transit Gateway with documented routing examples.
  - On-prem mode: installer accepts an offline bundle; no external downloads required.
- Security: mTLS for all control traffic; BYOK support for model keys; audit export to customer endpoint.
- Functionality: ability to pin model versions, perform canary rollouts, and automatic fallback to hosted variant.
- Observability: metrics, request traces, and per-route token cost visible locally and exported to Prometheus / Pushgateway.
- Performance: end-to-end median latency within X% of hosted baseline under the customer's baseline network (TBD).

Jamal Singh: Edge cases to call out: split-horizon DNS causing control plane to resolve differently; asymmetric routing breaking TLS session affinity; MTU fragmentation for large token streams; customers behind HTTP proxies requiring CONNECT. Also cert rotation when nodes are in different maintenance windows. Add acceptance tests for these.

Sophie Park: Runbook asks:
- Default firewall rules (egress to control plane 443 + customer SIEM endpoint), sample terraform + iptables snippet.
- Instructions for enabling audit log streaming and rotating keys.
- Escalation: steps to revert to hosted fallback and notify customer.

Kevin Ortiz: Test checklist proposal (short):
1) Deploy in test VPC + PrivateLink endpoint, verify control-plane API responds.
2) Run model pin + canary (10% traffic) and validate inference correctness.
3) Kill node, verify KV cache warmup and no HPA cascading failures.
4) Validate no plaintext secrets in logs and KMS encrypts tokens at rest.

Maria Chen: Sample networking snippet for customers (we'll include in RFC):
```hcl
resource "aws_vpc_endpoint" "redwood_control" {
  service_name = "com.amazonaws.vpce.us-west-2.vpce-svc-xxxxxxxx"
  vpc_id       = var.vpc_id
  subnet_ids   = var.subnet_ids
  private_dns_enabled = true
}
```

Jamal Singh: Acceptance criteria must include auditability: every control-plane operation has a log entry with user, action, timestamp, affected-resources, and request-id. Logs must be exportable in JSON and LTC (syslog) formats. Also include dead-man's switch hooks if KMS rotates unexpectedly.

infra-bot: RFC draft created: https://internal.docs/redwood/private-deploy-networking-rfc (draft) — owners: @Maria Chen, @Jamal Singh.

Alex Rivera: Good first pass — please add the explicit rollback and canary metrics (error rate, latency, token-cost delta). Also include a short acceptance test for 'no internet' air-gapped installs (installer validates bundle checksums + embedded CA). I'll consolidate into PRD after comments. Deadline: Friday EOD. Owners: Maria (networking + installer), Jamal (security + KMS), Kevin (runtime tests), Sophie (customer docs).

Maria Chen: I'll update the RFC with the acceptance checklist, sample terraform, and the MTU/proxy edge-case tests by tomorrow noon.

Kevin Ortiz: I'll add the runtime perf targets and a small load harness for canary testing (gRPC + WS).

Sophie Park: I'll draft the customer-facing runbook and the terraform examples.

Jamal Singh: I'll enumerate PKCS#11 providers we test with and the HSM integration acceptance tests.

Alex Rivera: Thanks all — ping me if anything blocks the Friday ship. :thumbsup:
